clue.text: East European collects bill for drinking

indicators.note: the Pole gathers the bill into himself, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a Pole is a native of Poland in Eastern Europe
a tab is a bill, as in a bar tab

explanation.surface: An Eastern European visitor picks up the bill for a round of drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Potable water is water that is safe and fit to drink.

clue.text: Pistols rating success in the charts

parts.note: pops are guns, a slang word for pistols
a tar is a sailor, a rating in the navy

explanation.surface: The Sex Pistols' rating in the charts was a success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pistols' calls up the punk band, but here it means guns.
explanation.definitionFit: A pop star is a performer whose records do well in the hit parade.

clue.text: Know they're upset by daily

indicators.note: the letters of Know they're are upset into a new order

parts.note: times means by, as in three by four

explanation.surface: People who know are upset by a daily newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: KNOW THEY'RE rearranged gives THE NEW YORK, then TIMES.
explanation.definitionFit: The New York Times is a newspaper published every day.

clue.text: Good luck playing Akela, bizarrely, in production of 1984?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the other piece

parts.note: a car produced in 1984 in Britain carried a B reg, B registration plate

indicators.note: Akela is jumbled bizarrely into a new order

explanation.surface: Wishing good luck to a cub leader acting in a staging of Orwell's 1984.
explanation.walkthrough: '1984' suggests Orwell's novel, but it is the year of a car: British number plates registered then began with B, so a B REG. Akela is the leader of a Cub Scout pack.
explanation.definitionFit: Break a leg is the theatrical idiom wishing an actor luck before a performance.

clue.text: Put restriction in place as lawyer goes to prove cases

definitions.text: Put restriction in place as lawyer

indicators.note: the words goes to prove act as a case holding the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A lawyer imposes a restriction as he goes on to prove his cases.
explanation.definitionFit: Estop is a legal term meaning to bar or preclude a party by estoppel.

clue.text: Jabber disjointedly, yes — about nothing, apparently

indicators.note: the rearranged yes goes round the other piece, enclosing it
the word yes is taken apart and its letters set out in a new order

parts.note: a ring looks like the figure 0, so it is apparently nothing

explanation.surface: Someone babbles a disconnected yes about nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jabber' looks like a verb meaning babble, but here it is the thing that gives you a jab.
explanation.definitionFit: A syringe is the needle device a nurse uses to give a jab, hence a jabber.

clue.text: Ace, retired, brought in to keep watch on flat? Get me!

indicators.note: the two abbreviations are brought into the word for keep watch

parts.note: to spy is to keep watch
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards
re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: A retired flying ace is brought in to keep watch over a flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' is a punctured tyre, and 'Get me!' is the boast of a paunch: a spare tyre is also a roll of belly fat.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare tyre is the replacement wheel you fit after a puncture, and slang for a fat midriff.

clue.text: On debut, girl unfortunately appears in split dress

indicators.note: the letters appear inside the word for split

parts.note: a rip is a split or tear

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so each word gives its first letter

explanation.surface: On her debut a girl unluckily appears in a torn dress.
explanation.definitionFit: To rig up or rig out is to clothe or kit someone out.

clue.text: Seeing it sickens, I politely decline rather large number

parts.note: no, ta is a polite refusal, ta being British for thanks
pretty means rather, as in pretty good
a sight is informal for a lot, as in a sight more

explanation.surface: Someone politely refuses a rather large number of something that makes them ill.
explanation.walkthrough: Ta is British informal for thank you, so 'No, ta' declines politely.
explanation.definitionFit: Not a pretty sight describes something unpleasant or revolting to look at.

clue.text: Regulars departing better hurry in an ancient part of Italy

indicators.note: one set of regular, alternate letters departs and the other alternate letters remain

explanation.surface: Regular customers leave, told to hurry up in an old corner of Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on of 'better hurry in an'.
explanation.definitionFit: Etruria was the ancient region of central Italy home to the Etruscans.

clue.text: Fed with line, not like anything in a Coward play

indicators.note: the run of letters is placed inside the word standing for a

parts.note: per means a, as in five pounds per head

indicators.note: the line is fed in between the two words either side of it

parts.note: to resent something is not to like it
aught is an old word for anything

explanation.surface: A play by Noel Coward seems to be described as fed with a line and disliked by all.
explanation.walkthrough: Per in the sense 'a' (five pounds a head) is the easily missed container. Noel Coward was an English playwright and actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Present Laughter is a 1939 comedy written by Noel Coward, so it is one of his stage plays.

clue.text: Provocatively dance tango with airman

parts.note: T is Tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet
erk is RAF slang for an aircraftman of the lowest rank

explanation.surface: A sultry tango danced with a pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: An erk is British slang for the lowest rank of aircraftman in the Royal Air Force.
explanation.definitionFit: Twerking is dancing with sexually provocative thrusting hip movements.

clue.text: Sheeran takes offence with support accommodating beguiling musician

indicators.note: the support houses the other letters within it

parts.note: a pier is a pillar supporting a bridge
Ed Sheeran is the English pop singer
the pip is a fit of annoyance, as in to give someone the pip

explanation.surface: Ed Sheeran takes umbrage while a backing act hosts a charming player.
explanation.walkthrough: To give someone the pip is British slang for annoying them, so the pip is offence taken.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pied Piper of Hamelin lured the town's rats and then its children away with his enchanting pipe music.

clue.text: Blues defenders all at sea

parts.note: royal blue and navy blue are both blues, and the force they name defends Britain on the oceans

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a football side with a hopeless back four. But the two blues, royal and navy, together name the sea service.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Navy is Britain's naval force, which defends the country at sea.

clue.text: Titular changeling has accepted being divine

indicators.note: the words Titular changeling have accepted the answer and hold it inside

explanation.surface: A changeling in a story's title has been taken for a god.
explanation.definitionFit: An archangel is an angel of high rank, a heavenly being.

clue.text: Artist's mother and child eye detail on arrivals board

parts.note: a private eye is a PI, a private investigator
ETA, estimated time of arrival, is shown on an arrivals board

explanation.surface: Someone's eye catches a detail on the airport arrivals board.
explanation.definitionFit: A pieta is a painting or sculpture of the Virgin Mary holding the dead Christ, her son, in her lap.

clue.text: Father and son see badly cooked goose, in the end

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father

indicators.note: son and see are badly arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A father and son can see that the goose was overcooked by the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' sits beside 'badly' as if part of the anagram signal, but it belongs to the definition: the pope's nose is the rear of a cooked bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The pope's nose is the fatty rump at the tail of a roast bird.

clue.text: Shilling for good kid

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for a shilling, the old British coin
pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: Paying a shilling to a good child.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprog is British slang for a young child or baby.

clue.text: Chief of Staff overseeing post, greenlight whip in Cape Town

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece overseeing another sits above it
the chief letter of staff is its first

parts.note: a jamb is the upright post of a door frame
to OK something is to give it the green light

explanation.surface: The chief of staff oversees the post and gives approval for the whip in Cape Town.
explanation.definitionFit: A sjambok is a heavy leather whip used in South Africa.

clue.text: Queen's gallery exhibits a Constable retrospective, entertaining stars

indicators.note: the reversed letters play host to the stars, which go within them
a retrospective looks back, so these letters are read from the end

parts.note: art is what a gallery holds
PC is a police constable
Leo is a constellation, a group of stars

explanation.surface: The Queen's Gallery puts on a retrospective of John Constable's art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constable' looks like the painter, but it is a police officer. ART, A and PC read backwards give CPATRA, which takes in LEO.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra was the last ruling monarch of Ptolemaic Egypt.

clue.text: Flavouring also stays with you!

indicators.note: the word for also stays, holding in place the other piece

parts.note: and means also
I see means I'm with you, I understand

explanation.surface: A flavour that lingers, staying with you.
explanation.walkthrough: I SEE goes inside AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Aniseed is the liquorice-tasting seed of anise used to flavour sweets and drinks.

clue.text: Original in album that group playing has taken time to pen?

definitions.text: Original in album that group playing has taken time to pen?

indicators.note: the anagram encloses the letter, as a pen encloses animals
the letters are played about with into a new order
the time is taken away from the letters
the original letter in album is its first

explanation.surface: A band member signs an album, taking time to write a signature.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue also describes the signed item a fan holds, so it works as definition too.
explanation.definitionFit: An autograph is a signature written by hand in an autograph book or album.

clue.text: Author now showing advanced years? Not one of them

indicators.note: not means the letter for a year is left out

parts.note: greyer describes hair that shows age
Y is the abbreviation for year, one of the years

explanation.surface: An author now shows her age, but not one of the years.
explanation.walkthrough: GREYER loses a Y (year). Germaine Greer wrote The Female Eunuch.
explanation.definitionFit: Germaine Greer is the Australian writer famous for The Female Eunuch.

clue.text: As the hour's moved on, you'll have to run to make it

definitions.text: you'll have to run to make it

indicators.note: the hour's letter is shifted to a new position in the phrase

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: As time moves on, you'll need to run to get there.
explanation.walkthrough: The H of AS THE moves from the middle to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Making haste means hurrying, which you do by running.

clue.text: Treat endlessly knocked back — can it lead to indigestion?

definitions.text: Treat endlessly knocked back — can it lead to indigestion?

indicators.note: knocked back means read the other way round
the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to use someone badly is to treat them badly
sh is the call for quiet, can it

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A diner wonders whether a dish knocked back too fast causes indigestion.
explanation.walkthrough: USE loses its end to give US, read backwards SU; then SH and the first letter of indigestion. The whole clue also asks about raw fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese delicacy of vinegared rice with raw fish, a treat that might upset a stomach.

clue.text: I asked questions, being worried about warning given by energy firm

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit about the others, enclosing them
being is worried into a new arrangement of its letters

parts.note: an amber traffic light is a warning
gas is a form of energy
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Someone frets over the warning letter from their gas supplier.
explanation.walkthrough: An amber traffic light warns drivers. Bamber Gascoigne hosted the British TV quiz University Challenge for 25 years.
explanation.definitionFit: Bamber Gascoigne was the quizmaster of University Challenge, so his job was putting questions.

clue.text: Attacker from above strikes Trelawny's heart

indicators.note: the answer lies in the heart of the words strikes Trelawny, inside them

explanation.surface: Someone strikes at the heart of a man called Trelawny.
explanation.definitionFit: A kestrel is a falcon that hovers before diving down on its prey.

clue.text: With a change of sides built in

indicators.note: the side right swaps to the side left, so R becomes L

parts.note: erected means built

explanation.surface: Something was built in with its sides changed round.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) in ERECTED is replaced by L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: A politician who is in has won office, having been voted into power.
